title: Automated passive-activation runbooks and failover operator (Terraform + Helm)
author: Priya Nair
release_notes: Adds automated passive-activation runbooks and a failover operator; introduces Terraform module for passive activation workflows; Helm chart for operator and canary probes; improves DR tests and monitoring alerts; no breaking changes to installer API.
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private in multi-AZ or on-prem clusters need a documented, automatable path to bring standby clusters from passive to active with minimal manual steps during controlled drills or unexpected failovers. This PR implements an operator + runbook-as-code approach that automates the passive-to-active activation path, wires it into Terraform/Hem workflows, and provides safe rollback and validation checks. Summary of changes: 1) New Kubernetes operator (passive-activation-operator) deployed via Helm; operator watches ClusterActivation CR and orchestrates DNS switch, PVC promotion, and leader election handoff with pre/post validation hooks. 2) Terraform module terraform/modules/passive_activation implements an opinionated orchestration plan for runbook-triggered resources (Route53 records, load balancer policies, IAM role bindings) and exposes input variables for safe gating. 3) Helm chart updates (helm/charts/private-installer) to include failover-operator, canary readiness probes and an optional maintenance-mode flag. 4) Runbooks-as-code (docs/runbooks/passive-activation.md) with a one-command dry-run and an audited execution path that writes to the installer audit log. 5) Integration tests and an Ansible proof-of-concept playbook for air-gapped environments. Rollout plan: feature is disabled by default; operator chart is optional in private-installer values. We validated in a staging multi-AZ cluster with a staged promotion: (a) DNS split, (b) write-path gating via leader lease, (c) short-lived read-only window for clients, (d) controlled traffic cutover. Safety controls: soft-fail safeties, automatic rollback on health-check regression, audit trail and a post-mortem hook to collect metrics and KV cache snapshots. Backwards compatibility: the module and chart are opt-in; existing private installs that do not enable the operator are unaffected. Testing and CI: added unit tests for operator reconciliation, terraform validate pipeline, helm lint, and a DR smoke integration job that runs a canary promotion in a teardown environment. Known limitations: current operator assumes cloud DNS provider or compatible on-prem DNS automation; full LDAP/AD integration is out of scope for this PR and will be addressed in follow-ups. References: ENG-5891 for design, ENG-6050 for monitoring requirements, SUP-4132 for the customer incident that motivated this work.

notes_for_ops: Operator disabled by default. To enable, set helm value 'passiveActivation.enabled=true' and provide dns and lease controller settings. Terraform module must be applied with plan review; use 'dry_run=true' for first rehearsals. Audit logs are written to installer/audit namespace; post-cutover artifacts stored in s3-compatible bucket if configured.
